messages.author: 396b75d7716eb3d9
messages.subject: question about spde model
parts:
Hi,

I am new to SPDE model.  I use formula <- y~-1 + Intercept + x1 + f(field, model=spde). 
I am not clear what is stored in res$summary.linear.predictor, since it contains Apredictor.001...Apredictor.100 and Predictor.001...Predictor.200. I think Apredictor is for linear predictor. Some of Predictor are also for the linear predictor. Does any one tell me what the remaining part of Predictor is for?

Thanks,
Lynn

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] question about spde model
parts:
A.predictor is the A-matrix times the predictor (ie what the likelihood sees). This is usually what you want. 

Dan

messages.subject: Re: question about spde model
parts:
Do you mean PredictorXXX is the linear predictor without A-matrix? I found some of the values in Predictor XXX are the same as in ApredictorXXX, while some are different which I do not know how they come?
e.g. i use the following code
formula <- y~-1 + Intercept + x1 + f(field, model=spde).

res=inla(formula,
         data=inla.stack.data(stack,spde=spde),
         family="gaussian",
         control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack),
                                compute=TRUE))

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: question about spde model
parts:
I suggest comparing the two vectors
A %*% Predictor
and
Apredictor

Hopefully these are the same numbers. Where A=inla.stack.A(stack). If the A-matrix is the identity, these will be exactly the same.

Kind regards,
Haakon

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: question about spde model
parts:
Note that they will never be _exactly_ the same, for several reasons, including
*) finite precision floating point numerics
*) for fitted.values with a nonlinear link function, h(A*x) is not equal to A*h(x)

Finn

Finn
